standard_prerequisites.name: The category of derived complete objects of D(A) with respect to an ideal I is closed under the derived limit of an inverse system
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 26297-26298 as a standing property of derived complete objects
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the assertion for the derived limit K' to the assertion for each of the objects K tensor^L K_n.

standard_prerequisites.name: The vanishing of the derived torsion functor T(-, f) on an object is equivalent to f being locally nilpotent on that object, so an object killed by a power of f is derived complete with respect to the principal ideal generated by f
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 26299-26301, where the assumption that f^e is zero on K tensor^L K_n is turned into T(K tensor^L K_n, f) = 0
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that each term of the system is derived complete with respect to I, one generator at a time, which finishes the proof after the reduction.

core_obligations: Set K' equal to the derived limit of the objects K tensor^L K_n and reduce to the individual terms: because the derived complete objects form a category closed under derived limits, it suffices to prove that each K tensor^L K_n is derived complete with respect to I (proof lines 26296-26298).

Use the hypothesis that for every f in I and every n there is an exponent e with f^e zero on K_n to conclude that f^e is also zero on K tensor^L K_n, for every generator f of I (proof lines 26299-26300).

Conclude that the torsion functor T(K tensor^L K_n, f) vanishes for every f in I, which is precisely the criterion for that object to be derived complete with respect to I, and hence finish the proof (proof lines 26300-26301).
proof_roadmap: Observe that derived completeness is preserved under the derived limit, so it is enough to treat a single K tensor^L K_n (proof lines 26297-26298).
Transport the annihilation hypothesis from K_n to K tensor^L K_n and read it as the vanishing of the torsion functor for each element of the ideal (proof lines 26299-26301).
Quote the criterion that vanishing of the torsion functors is exactly derived completeness and close the argument (proof lines 26300-26301).
difficulty_reason: The statement takes a ring A, an ideal I and an inverse system of objects K_n of D(A) on which every element f of I acts nilpotently in the sense that some power of f is zero on K_n, and asserts that for every K the derived limit of the objects K tensor^L K_n is derived complete with respect to I (statement lines 26287-26294). The proof proceeds by reducing along the two structural facts of the theory: derived complete objects are closed under derived limits, so the limit may be replaced by its terms, and the vanishing of the torsion functor is the criterion for derived completeness, so the nilpotence assumption on K_n gives the result term by term after tensoring with K (proof lines 26296-26301). The argument is short but complete, and it is the concatenation of the two reductions that makes the statement work with no finiteness hypothesis on K.
